description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) changes as the co-occurrence number increases, with six method curves shown in a shared coordinate system. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\) (no explicit units shown). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 60 to 85 with labeled ticks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” line is black with circular markers and a solid style, rising from about 66 at \(10^1\) to about 83 near \(10^3\). The “FT” line is blue with downward-pointing triangle markers and a solid style, increasing from about 67 at \(10^1\) to about 84 near \(10^3\). The “IKE” line is red with upward-pointing triangle markers and a solid style, increasing from about 69 at \(10^1\) to about 86 near \(10^3\). The “MEMIT” line is purple with pentagon-like markers and a solid style, increasing from about 71 at \(10^1\) to about 88 near \(10^3\). The “MEND” line is brown with diamond markers and a solid style, increasing from about 73 at \(10^1\) to about 90 near \(10^3\). The “ROME” line is green with square markers and a solid style, increasing from about 76 at \(10^1\) to about 92 near \(10^3\), with all lines showing upward trends across the plotted x-range.
